note: GLOBALCIT's Citizenship Law Dataset v3.0 (EUI, 2025), coding the law in force on 1 January 2024 (A06a Const 12(2)(a), BRA 65; A06b Const 12(2)(a), BRA 65; L05 No provision): ordinary naturalisation after 4 years' residence; no renunciation of other citizenships required; a citizen keeps it on taking another. Reforms after that date are checked in the file's later sources, where a later source is given. Citizenship at birth is read from the same dataset's 2024 coding of modes A01a (descent, born in country: No provision), A01b (descent, born abroad: Generational transmission restriction: conditional on birthplace/place of residence /mode under which parent acquired citizenship), A02a (birth in country: Generally applicable provision) and A02b (birth in country to a parent born there: No provision), as its codebook (RSC/GLOBALCIT 2025/01, sections 3.2.1a to 3.2.2b) defines them: by birth in the territory unconditionally; by descent from either parent, a child born abroad on the limit the dataset states (the dataset codes no separate descent rule for a child born in the country, birth there giving it; the parent's sex is read from mode A01b). Changes to the law at birth after 1 January 2024 weren't checked for this file. No fee is charged for naturalisation under current law, and the procedure must end within 180 days of the request (Decree 9,199/2017 art. 228, as the Ministry of Justice's questions page quotes it); the applicant must be able to communicate in Portuguese, shown by Celpe-Bras or an approved course and at the Federal Police interview (Ministry of Justice, ordinary naturalisation). No civics test is asked.
